notes.title: Dev Diary #20 - Bug Fixes, Boons & Banes
notes.notes:
Hi all!

It has been a minute since the last update, but I'm working on getting things moving faster again!

[list]
[*] FIX: There were a number of minor bugs that cascaded into a bigger overall problem with the in-game event resolution system. When a random event occurs, things should actually take effect when the player responds to it.
[*] FIX: A couple in-game events had mismatched event effects and conditions.
[*] CHANGE: Show each party member's last name in addition to their first name in the journal
[*] NEW FEATURE (WIP): I'm adding a new system for buffing or de-buffing the player's party overall for a given amount of time. The effects can for now either boost or reduce health and/or morale! For example, the [i]Clear Weather[/i] event slightly raises the party's health and morale for a short period of time.
[*] OTHER: I'm continuing to work on end game functionality like different UI screens and implementation
[/list]

I have since moved on to Bluesky for all social media updates! Feel free to follow me there! :)
https://bsky.app/profile/starcatgames.ltd


Thanks for reading!
- C

notes.title: Dev Diary #19 - A Bunch of Changes!
notes.notes:
Hi all!

[list]
[*] COMPLETED: The fishing mini-game is now what I consider "complete"! I'll no doubt make some changes to it in the future, but it'll do the job for now. There are currently 3 obstacle layouts where you launch a ball in an attempt to land it in the catcher at the bottom, which randomly positions itself when you start. I'll add more variety in future updates!
[*] NEW FEATURE: I've added new achievements for traveling the various biomes across the world map!
[*] NEW FEATURE: Food consumption! While I still need to add and test values for different food items, party members should now eat food while traveling to stay healthy (and happy)!
[*] IN-PROGRESS: Work continues on the travel logic concerning health and treatment tracking. Being able to easily tell the state of your party members is important, and I need to polish that aspect up yet.
[/list]

notes.title: Dev Diary #11 - Unity Engine Update & Steam Rich Presence
notes.notes:
Hi all!

[h3]Unity Engine Update[/h3]

I finally sorted out the issues I was having with various shaders, assets, and what not in getting Unity updated. The game is now running on version [b]2022.3[/b], up from [b]2020.3[/b]. Getting weather effects, various materials, water shading, and camera stacking all working was something of a nightmare, but it seems to all be happy again. The benefit here is that the game isn't stuck years in the past as far as the engine goes, gaining any and all bug fixes, performance improvements, etc. Some of the assets I'm using have stopped supporting Unity 2020 so it was getting to the point where it was becoming an issue.

[h3]Steam Rich Presence[/h3]

A new feature is integration with Steam Rich Presence, so you/your friends will be able to see what's going on with via your Steam status when playing:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43607312/cd5e8cc6e41a699f8a0f2398675f8fd8039c84cc.png[/img]

And finally, I've made some improvements to the build automation tools I'm using so it's easier to track build changes going forward.

Thanks!
- C

notes.title: Dev Diary #01 - Tile Inventory System, Bug Fixes & Steam Integration
notes.notes:
Hi all!

This week was mostly bug-fixing & cleaning up things here and there. Up next I think I'll tackle some of the UI for viewing and managing party health, such as treatments for injuries and sicknesses.

I first wrote the tile-based inventory for the exploration side of the game over a year ago, and have been putting off fixing some long-standing bugs. Namely issues with rotating asymmetrical items like the rifle shown below (4x1). Luckily most of the issues I had were easy enough to fix once I dug into it.

The core concept is that you can bring items with you from your party's inventory when you go exploring. For example, you could bring a rifle and ammo along for hunting. On the other side of the coin is being able to bring things back with you when you're done. Collecting things like meat, plants, fish, and valuables will help keep your journey moving smoothly.

The limit to what you can carry will be determined by two things: your [b]weight capacity[/b], and what you can fit on your person via [b]the tiles[/b]. Certain tile zones will only allow certain types of items. Such as in the image below, the rifle will only be allowed to be carried in the backpack or shoulder tiles, and only small items can fit in the pockets.

A to-do item is to visually indicate where items can be dropped while dragging them so it's not just a guessing game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43607312/627fcac2b64b58029f0a868db3070079169f6e61.gif[/img]

The other semi-major change is finally getting an implementation of hooking into Steam's API, mostly for [b]achievements[/b], but also just to get events and info from Steam.

That's all I've got this time around, thanks for reading!

- C

[u][b]Steam:[/b][/u]

Wire into it with simple singleton class in the GameCore.
Flush changes for newly acquired achievements so they register right away.

[u][b]Exploration:[/b][/u]
Fix PerimeterSlots never being cleared properly in a TileSlot.
Fix TileSlot opacity being reset when it was a perimeter but became the root (ShiftDrag).
Fix issue in the TileInventoryController where ColumnCount was no longer being updated correctly because the Tile size changed.
Add external inventory as a TileInventoryController so items can fall back to there if they can't fit in the player's inventory.
Fixed bug where self-intersections of Tile perimeter slots would cause a Tile drag to fail in inventory UI.
